column1: Raising investment funds by issuing bonds is called debt finance, and raising funds by issuing stock is called equity finance. Debt and equity are forms of direct finance because the saver knows whose investment project his funds are financing. Another piece of the financial system is the set of financial intermediaries through which households can indirectly provide resources for investment. As the term suggests, a financial intermediary stands between the two sides of the market and helps move financial resources toward their best use. Commercial banks are the best-known type of financial intermediary. They take deposits from savers and use these deposits to make loans to those who have investment projects they need to finance. Other examples of financial intermediaries include mutual funds, pension funds, and insurance companies. When an intermediary is involved, the financing is considered indirect because the saver is often unaware of whose investments his funds are financing.
